name: Mary Sutherland
story: Mary Sutherland (1893–1955) was a forester and botanist who became New Zealand’s first woman appointed to a professional forestry position in the State Forest Service in 1923. She had already become the first woman in the United Kingdom to complete a forestry BSc. Restrictions on mixed field accommodation limited her assignments in New Zealand, so much of her early work involved technical calculations, plantation records and microscopic studies of conifers. She researched pine-leaf structure and participated in the New Zealand Institute of Foresters.

After retrenchment in 1932, Sutherland worked at the Dominion Museum. In 1946 she became the Department of Agriculture’s farm forestry officer, planning plantings and advising on farm shelter belts and woodlots. Her work belongs to the surveying, inventory and land-management practices that preceded computerised forestry mapping; the available biography does not attribute GIS work to her.
